m1_zero_omission_notes.chapter_executive_summary: Introduces sequences where each term is obtained by adding a fixed common difference 'd' to the preceding term, deriving formulas for the nth term an = a + (n-1)d and sum of n terms Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d].

detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 5.1 Definition & General Term of an AP
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: An AP is a list of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a constant d to the preceding term. General form: a, a+d, a+2d, ... nth term: an = a + (n-1)d.

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: an = a + (n - 1)d, where a is first term and d is common difference.

detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 5.2 Sum of First n Terms of an AP
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d] or Sn = n/2 [a + l], where l is the last term.

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: Carl Friedrich Gauss summed 1 to 100 instantly as a boy by pairing terms (1+100, 2+99...).

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: The fixed difference between consecutive terms of an AP: d = a_(k+1) - a_k.
An AP containing a finite number of terms, possessing a clear last term.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Sum of First n Terms
formulas_rules_and_laws.variable_definitions: a = first term, d = common difference, n = number of terms, l = last term

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.activity_or_procedure_title: Determining if a Sequence forms an AP
step_by_step_procedure: Since d is not constant, sequence is NOT an AP.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.scientific_or_logical_conclusion: Requires constant d to be an AP.

m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.frequent_student_error: Confusing an (nth term value) with n (term position number).
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.root_cause: Semantic confusion between position and value.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.correct_approach: n must always be a positive integer representing position; an is the actual numerical value at that position.
